clue.text: Lo-cal filling for entourage shows civility

indicators.note: a filling sits inside something else, so the first item is packed into the second

parts.note: a posse is a celebrity's crowd of hangers-on
lite is the American labelling for low-calorie food

explanation.surface: A diet sandwich served to a star's hangers-on proves how polite the host is.
explanation.walkthrough: Lite is the American spelling used on low-calorie food labels, and a posse is a celebrity's crowd of hangers-on.
explanation.definitionFit: Politesse is a formal, French-derived word for courteous good manners.

clue.text: Magazine for child actor?

parts.note: an actor is one who plays; the question mark admits the stretch
a boy is a male child

explanation.surface: Asking which publication suits a young performer.
explanation.walkthrough: A child actor is a boy who plays, read in reverse order as PLAY + BOY; hardly a magazine for children.
explanation.definitionFit: Playboy is the famous American men's magazine founded by Hugh Hefner.

clue.text: Delay help? Limitless fraud is on the rise in airport

parts.note: a lag is a delay

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means reading from bottom to top, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: aid means help

indicators.note: without limits means its boundary letters at each end are dropped

parts.note: the word with its first and last letters gone

explanation.surface: Fraud is increasing at an airport, and the delays are no help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'help' and the trimmed 'fraud' together are read upward. LaGuardia is one of New York City's airports.
explanation.definitionFit: LaGuardia is a major commercial airport in Queens, New York City.

clue.text: Jackson, found in rowboat, went yonder

indicators.note: something found in a phrase is lying inside it, so the answer sits within the words that follow

parts.note: runs across the end of the boat word, the whole of the verb, and the start of the last word

explanation.surface: Somebody named Jackson was spotted in a rowboat heading off into the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Jackson's portrait is on the US twenty-dollar bill, so 'a Jackson' is American slang for a twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang a Jackson is a twenty-dollar bill, after the president pictured on its face.

clue.text: Present wrapped in San Francisco, Geneva and Winnipeg — they're all different

definitions.note: a clause describing the plural answer rather than a noun

indicators.note: a present wrapped in something is enclosed by it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the usual abbreviation for the city
present as in the current moment
Lake Geneva and Lake Winnipeg are both lakes

explanation.surface: A gift is posted in three cities, and each city is unlike the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift; it is the time sense. Geneva and Winnipeg are cities that are also lakes. S(NOW)F + LAKES.
explanation.definitionFit: Folk wisdom says no two snowflakes are ever alike, so every one is unique.

clue.text: Give out online university in Cambridge?

parts.note: E, as in e-mail, stands for electronic or online
the Massachusetts Institute of Technology is in Cambridge, Massachusetts

explanation.surface: A query about whether an English university hands out degrees over the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge suggests the English university; the question mark points to Cambridge, Massachusetts instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or discharge, such as light, heat or sound.

clue.text: Settle in Pennsylvania? You betcha

parts.note: the postal abbreviation for the state
a casual American yes, just like 'you betcha'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to put down roots in Pennsylvania and gets an enthusiastic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle in Pennsylvania' looks like moving house, but settle here means clearing a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay up is to settle a bill or debt by handing over the money owed.

clue.text: Writing about border flower

indicators.note: about means around, so the first item goes round the second

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: An essay about the plants in a garden border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border flower' reads as a gardening phrase, but the border is the inserted piece. P(RIM)ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose is a pale yellow spring wildflower common in hedgerows.

clue.text: What bakers need is votes for a bit of torte

parts.note: yea votes are votes in favour

indicators.note: a small bit of a word here means just its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the cake

explanation.surface: Bakers are voting on who gets a slice of cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is the fungus bakers use to make bread dough rise.

clue.text: "Father knows best," in a way

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
read as ''s sage', is wise, with 's short for is

explanation.surface: The title of the 1950s sitcom, said to be true in a certain way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father knows best' becomes "Pa's sage", father is wise. 'Father Knows Best' was a 1950s US family sitcom.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a way through, such as a corridor or channel.

clue.text: Fish's point of view

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to try to catch fish with a rod and line
second meaning: a particular way of looking at an issue

explanation.surface: How the world looks from the perspective of a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive invites you to imagine a fish's outlook; really the 's just joins two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To angle is to go fishing with hook and line, and an angle is also a slant or perspective.

clue.text: Tattered rags in oil: what you might feed into a photocopier

definitions.text: what you might feed into a photocopier

indicators.note: something tattered is torn apart, so the following letters are ripped up and rearranged

parts.note: these nine letters are the raw material

explanation.surface: Torn, oily rags are not something to push through an office copier.
explanation.definitionFit: Originals are the master documents you place in a copier to produce duplicates.

clue.text: Skinner to take in last of launch

indicators.note: to take something in is to let it inside, so one piece ends up wrapped by another

parts.note: B. F. Skinner was the American behavioural psychologist
these two words are used exactly as they stand

explanation.surface: A man called Skinner is told to absorb the final part of a rocket launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of launch' begs you to take the final letter H; instead 'last of' is used whole and 'launch' is the definition. B(LAST OF)F.
explanation.definitionFit: Blast-off is the moment a rocket leaves the ground, the launch itself.

clue.text: Eartha dancing with soul singer

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about and change places

parts.note: the first name of the singer Eartha Kitt, used as letters

explanation.surface: Eartha Kitt takes to the dance floor alongside a soul star.
explanation.walkthrough: One diva's first name rearranges into another's: Aretha Franklin, the Queen of Soul.
explanation.definitionFit: Aretha Franklin was the celebrated American soul vocalist known by her first name alone.

clue.text: Extremely aristocratic teen gets unhinged when taking train

indicators.note: taking in means holding within, so a piece is inserted
something unhinged is off its hinges and in disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the eight letters to be scrambled
the El is the elevated railway, in Chicago or old New York

explanation.surface: A snobbish teenager loses it when forced to ride the train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like a selection signal for first and last letters, but it belongs to the definition as the superlative.
explanation.definitionFit: Genteel means refined and well-bred, as an aristocrat would be; the superlative gives 'extremely'.

clue.text: Space creature contributes to Tokyo damage

indicators.note: the answer supplies part of the following words, so it lies inside them

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A monster from outer space helps wreck Tokyo, as in a Godzilla film.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoda is the small green alien Jedi master of the Star Wars films, set in space.

clue.text: Curt holds on to hat following Washington amusement-park ride

indicators.note: coming after means the next piece is placed behind the one named

parts.note: the postal abbreviation for Washington State

indicators.note: to hold on to something is to grip it inside, so one word sits within another

parts.note: curt and terse both mean brief to the point of rudeness
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A brusque man named Curt clutches his hat on a ride at a Washington theme park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curt' looks like a name; it is the adjective. WA + TERS(LID)E.
explanation.definitionFit: A water slide is a chute down which riders shoot into a pool, a staple of amusement parks.

clue.text: Author lives with a mob around court

parts.note: is means exists or lives

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece goes about the next

parts.note: a herd is a mob or crowd
to court someone is to woo them

explanation.surface: A writer resides alongside a crowd gathered round a courthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like a law court; it is the verb meaning romance. IS + HER(WOO)D.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Isherwood was the English-American novelist of 'Goodbye to Berlin'.

clue.text: Picking from nose one, two or three times? That's ridiculous

parts.note: surface reading: the childish habit of nose-picking
setter's reading: build a word using only the letters of the clue word, each picked once, twice or thrice

explanation.surface: Nose-picking, done once, twice or thrice? How absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: Pick letters from the word itself: N three times, O once, S and E twice each, and the result means 'rubbish!'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an exclamation dismissing something as absurd or untrue.

clue.text: Sculptor and soldier leading a reindeer — it is heading west

indicators.note: something leading goes in front, so these pieces are placed first in order

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
taken as written
Comet is one of Santa's reindeer

indicators.note: in an across answer going west means travelling right to left, so the word is turned around

parts.note: taken as written, then turned around

explanation.surface: An artist and a soldier lead a reindeer westward across the snow.
explanation.walkthrough: Comet is one of the reindeer in 'A Visit from St Nicholas' ('Twas the Night Before Christmas').
explanation.definitionFit: Alberto Giacometti was the Swiss artist famous for tall, thin bronze figures.

clue.text: Trash boat's prow in repair shop

indicators.note: in means placed inside the following item

parts.note: a garage repairs cars

indicators.note: a prow is the front of a vessel, so only the front letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the vessel

explanation.surface: Rubbish from the front of a boat ends up in the repair yard.
explanation.walkthrough: GAR(B)AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage is the American word for household waste or rubbish.

clue.text: Revolutionary female cook

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine Marxist revolutionary
F is the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman who cooks for the revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary female' reads as one person; it is two pieces, the guerrilla leader plus an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is a professional cook, especially one running a restaurant kitchen.

clue.text: Make one look good and less shiny…

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to show someone off to advantage, as clothes can
second meaning: the comparative of flat, as in a matte paint finish

explanation.surface: Advice on makeup: something that improves your looks and dulls the shine on your face.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis leads into the next clue only for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to enhance someone's appearance; as an adjective it is the comparative of flat, meaning more matte.

clue.text: …before company carves up plaster

indicators.note: before means placed ahead of the next piece
in a down answer up means reading from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: carves means cuts
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Continuing the makeover: before guests arrive, someone hacks at the wall plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine plaster used to coat walls and make decorative mouldings.

clue.text: Say no to 18 down

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to decline or turn down, a verb stressed on the second syllable
second meaning: the answer to 18 down, rubbish, a noun stressed on the first syllable

explanation.walkthrough: 18 down is GARBAGE; the two senses are spelt alike but pronounced differently.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to decline; as a noun it means waste matter thrown away.

clue.text: Beginning to feed group of birds as pets

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the verb
Aves is the scientific class that contains all birds

explanation.surface: Starting to feed a flock of birds kept as household animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pets' looks like animals; it means favourites, as in teacher's pet.
explanation.definitionFit: Faves is informal for favourites, and a favourite person is a pet, as in teacher's pet.

clue.text: Take another look at a place to stop

parts.note: to stare again: RE- meaning again plus stare meaning look at
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to revisit a spot where you might halt.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition hides behind the 'a': split the answer as RE-STARE A to see the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest area is a roadside lay-by on a highway where drivers pull over to take a break.

clue.text: Cry out, "Gee, a snake!"

parts.note: gee is the spoken name of the letter G
an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: Someone yelps in surprise at spotting a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gee' is an exclamation in the surface; it is the letter's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasp is a sudden sharp intake of breath, an involuntary exclamation of shock.

clue.text: Proverb involving wagon and Ford model's superiority

indicators.note: to involve is to include within, so the next items go inside the saying

parts.note: an adage is a traditional saying
a van is a covered wagon or vehicle
the Model T was Ford's famous early car

explanation.surface: An old saying about why a wagon and a Ford are better than other vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: The Model T was Henry Ford's mass-produced car of the early 1900s, so 'Ford model' is just the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An advantage is a superior position or a favourable edge over others.

clue.text: Slav's jacket, covering head of rooster…

indicators.note: a covering goes around something, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a coat is an outer garment like a jacket

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the bird

explanation.surface: An Eastern European's jacket keeps a rooster's head covered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slav's' reads as possessive, but the 's means 'is', joining definition to wordplay. CO(R)AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Croats are a South Slavic people of Croatia and neighbouring Balkan lands.

clue.text: …otherwise covers one cow

indicators.note: a thing that covers another surrounds it, so one piece wraps around the next

parts.note: else means otherwise, as in 'or else'
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Continuing the farmyard scene: otherwise, it is a cow that gets covered.
explanation.walkthrough: ELS(I)E. The ellipsis ties this to the previous clue only for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsie is the cartoon cow mascot of Borden dairy products in the United States, the best-known named cow.

clue.text: Attorney general goes after marijuana paraphernalia to avoid getting burned

indicators.note: going after means coming second, so this piece is placed behind the other

parts.note: pot is slang for marijuana
Eric Holder was US Attorney General when this puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: The nation's top lawyer pursues drug gear, being careful not to get burned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marijuana paraphernalia' reads as a unit (bongs, pipes); the second word belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A potholder is a padded cloth used to grip hot pans, kitchen gear that protects the hands from burns.
